about.title:
Six Decades of
Faith & Service
about.p1: Founded in 1963, the Conseil Protestant du Rwanda (CPR) is the umbrella body uniting Rwanda's 25 Protestant churches. Since its inception, CPR has been at the heart of Rwanda's social fabric — rebuilding communities after conflict, championing education, and upholding the dignity of every person.
about.p2Start: Today, through its departments in education, health, evangelism, and communications, CPR touches every province of Rwanda. Our motto —
about.motto: “Bose Babe Umwe” (That All of Them May Be One)

testimonials.desc: Hear from the individuals and communities whose lives have been touched by the work of the Conseil Protestant du Rwanda.

items.quote: The CPR scholarship program transformed my life. As a child of genocide survivors, I had no hope of attending university. Today I am a medical doctor serving my community.
Radio Inkoramutima reaches our village every morning. The trauma counseling programs on air have helped our whole congregation find peace and reconciliation.
Through the BNEP Active Pedagogy training, our teachers now create joyful classrooms where every child participates. Student performance has increased by 40% in two years.

whoWeAre.title: About Conseil Protestant du Rwanda
whoWeAre.p1: The Protestant Council of Rwanda (CPR) was established in 1963 to promote and share innovative development initiatives and deliver essential services to our member churches and the wider community.
whoWeAre.p2: We are committed to developing strong, impactful partnerships and providing world-class services to those we work with, fostering faith, unity, and sustainable development across Rwanda.

visionMission.title: Vision & Mission
visionMission.visionDesc: A united, faithful, and prosperous Rwandan society where every individual lives in dignity and peace.
visionMission.missionDesc: To bring together Protestant churches in Rwanda for a coordinated impact in evangelization, education, health, and holistic socio-economic development.

model.step1Desc: Protestant denominations across Rwanda unite under a shared framework.
model.step2Desc: Resources are mobilized through local contributions and international partnerships.
model.step3Desc: Sustainable, community-focused initiatives are deployed on the ground.

secretariatPage.heroDesc: The nerve centre of CPR — coordinating governance, events, advocacy, sustainability, and institutional communications across all member churches.
secretariatPage.introTitle: Coordinating the Protestant Council of Rwanda
secretariatPage.introDesc: The General Secretariat is the executive arm of CPR, responsible for implementing decisions of the General Assembly and the Executive Committee, managing inter-church relations, and representing CPR at national and international levels.

sgProfile.name: Rev. Samuel Mutabazi
sgProfile.title: Secretary General, Conseil Protestant du Rwanda
sgProfile.quote: The Protestant churches of Rwanda are called to be one — to serve together, witness together, and build this nation together. CPR exists to make that unity visible and effective in every corner of Rwanda.

meetings.title: Governance & Internal Meetings
meetings.desc: Beyond public events, CPR holds regular internal governance meetings that ensure accountability, strategic alignment, and effective coordination across all member churches and departments.
body: Executive Committee meetings — held quarterly to review institutional performance and approve key decisions
General Assembly sessions — the supreme governing body, convened annually with all 25 member churches
Bureau meetings — monthly coordination between the Secretary General and department heads
Finance and Audit Committee meetings — oversight of budgets, expenditures, and donor reporting
Inter-church coordination meetings — bilateral and multilateral dialogue between member denominations
Strategic planning retreats — annual sessions to review and update CPR's five-year strategic plan

sg.title: Office of the Secretary General
sg.desc: The Secretary General leads the day-to-day operations of CPR, serving as the chief executive officer of the Council and the primary liaison between member churches, government, and international partners.
body: Implements resolutions of the General Assembly and Executive Committee
Represents CPR in national and international forums and ecumenical bodies
Coordinates all departments and ensures institutional coherence
Manages human resources, legal affairs, and administrative operations
Maintains official correspondence and institutional memory
Oversees strategic planning and annual performance reporting

events.title: Conferences, Synods & Assemblies
events.desc: CPR convenes regular gatherings that bring together church leaders, government officials, civil society, and international partners to deliberate on matters of faith, governance, and national development.
body: Annual General Assembly of all 25 member churches
Biennial Synods for theological reflection and policy review
National prayer days and commemorative services (e.g. Kwibuka)
Ecumenical conferences with FECCLAHA and World Council of Churches
Leadership retreats and capacity-building workshops
Youth and women's assemblies for inclusive participation

advocacy.title: Policy Engagement & Civic Leadership
advocacy.desc: CPR actively engages Rwanda's public policy landscape, bringing the voice of the Protestant community to bear on issues of justice, human dignity, reconciliation, and national development.
body: Engagement with the Government of Rwanda on education, health, and social policy
Participation in the National Dialogue (Umushyikirano) and parliamentary consultations
Advocacy for genocide survivors, vulnerable communities, and marginalized groups
Promotion of reconciliation, unity, and peacebuilding across denominations
Collaboration with CNLG on genocide commemoration and memory preservation
Representation at the African Union and UN-level ecumenical platforms

sustainability.title: Environmental & Institutional Sustainability
sustainability.desc: CPR is committed to stewarding Rwanda's natural environment and building institutions that endure — integrating creation care into theology and ensuring long-term financial and organizational resilience.
body: Environmental theology programs integrated into church curricula
Tree-planting and land restoration initiatives across member churches
Green building standards promoted in CPR-affiliated schools and health centres
Institutional sustainability through diversified funding and endowment strategies
Partnerships with REMA and international environmental organizations
Annual sustainability reporting aligned with national green growth targets

publications.title: Reports, Newsletters & Communiqués
publications.desc: The Secretariat produces a range of official publications that document CPR's work, communicate institutional positions, and keep member churches and the public informed.
body: Annual Report — comprehensive review of CPR activities and financials
Quarterly Newsletter — updates from all departments and member churches
Official Communiqués — statements on national and ecumenical affairs
Theological Bulletins — reflections from the Secretary General and church leaders
Policy Briefs — position papers on education, health, and social issues
Kwibuka Memorial Publications — commemorative booklets and testimonies

cta.title: Get in Touch with the Secretariat
cta.desc: For official correspondence, partnership inquiries, or media requests, contact the Office of the Secretary General.
